statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-56289: GNU patch does not validate hunk line offsets in unified-diff input, so a crafted patch with an extremely large line number sends it into an effectively infinite loop. GNU patch through 2.8 is affected (CERT Polska, https://cert.pl/en/posts/2026/07/CVE-2026-56288/, which names the upstream fix https://cgit.git.savannah.gnu.org/cgit/patch.git/commit/?id=faba04ef4f2b410257f76c1b9dc85e350929c4b9: locate_hunk() in src/patch.c no longer treats a null-range hunk as an unconditional match). The GNU patch 2.8.1 release contains that change, and Alpine lists the CVE under 2.8.1-r0 in its 3.24-stable main/patch APKBUILD secfixes (https://gitlab.alpinelinux.org/alpine/aports/-/blob/3.24-stable/main/patch/APKBUILD). This owner's Alpine 3.24 builds are 2.8-r0, 2.8-r1, 2.8.1-r1 and 2.8.1-r2. Test used: a ten-line file and a one-line addition hunk headed @@ -99999999999,0 +99999999999,1 @@. On x86_64 and aarch64, /usr/bin/patch from 2.8-r0 and 2.8-r1 (GNU patch 2.8) was still running after 20 seconds and had to be killed, while 2.8.1-r1 and 2.8.1-r2 (GNU patch 2.8.1) applied the hunk at the end of the file at once. The range ends at 2.8.1-r1.

CVE-2026-56289: GNU patch does not validate hunk line offsets in unified-diff input, so a crafted patch with an extremely large line number sends it into an effectively infinite loop. GNU patch through 2.8 is affected (CERT Polska, https://cert.pl/en/posts/2026/07/CVE-2026-56288/, which names the upstream fix https://cgit.git.savannah.gnu.org/cgit/patch.git/commit/?id=faba04ef4f2b410257f76c1b9dc85e350929c4b9: locate_hunk() in src/patch.c no longer treats a null-range hunk as an unconditional match). Debian lists trixie as vulnerable (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-56289). The DHI Debian repository publishes two builds of patch for Debian 13, on amd64 and arm64: 2.8-2+deb13u0+dhi3, a rebuild of Debian's 2.8-2, and 2.8-2+deb13u1+dhi0, a rebuild of Debian's 2.8-2+deb13u1; both backport that upstream change. Test used: a ten-line file and a one-line addition hunk headed @@ -99999999999,0 +99999999999,1 @@. On amd64 and arm64, /usr/bin/patch from both builds applied the hunk at the end of the file at once, while Debian's own patch 2.8-2+deb13u1 on the same systems was still running after 20 seconds and had to be killed. Both builds' changelogs also record the backport. Every published build carries the fix, so the range ends at 2.8-2+deb13u0+dhi3, the lower of the two.
